role: The camp. Serves MUST #8 (day eject), #13 (portal arrival) and #14 (night: avoid 1 guard, soothe 2 sleepers), and after TASTE_GATE_T0_ASSETS Round 5 it is also where the companion is taken. This is the first spec to cover the camp; previously NO spec named it, which is the same coverage gap that hid the shrine defect (lintel on the ground, posts stacked) for the whole pipeline.

sequence.day: You stumble upon the camp IN DAYLIGHT. The companion is taken. You are ejected back to the homestead.
sequence.night: You take spirit form (bed AND rune), travel down, and use SPIRIT-STEALTH to reach the guards. You ease their suffering so they go to bed. Once they are in bed, you free the companion.
why_this_order_is_the_right_one: It uses the game's own day/night loop as the stakes. You LOSE them by day and GET them back by night, so the choice to become spirit is the strategic act rather than a menu tick.
It gives M8 a reason to exist. #8 was 'cartoon EJECT_HOME from day camp' with no cause; now it has one.
It makes the rescue two-stage instead of a walk. Reaching the guards and putting them to sleep is the work; freeing the companion is the reward.
sequence.the_one_guard_is_the_same_actor_twice: The single NODE_GUARD is what ejects you BY DAY (you were seen) and what you must avoid BY NIGHT (spirit-stealth). One actor, two tests, opposite solutions - be unseen by day, then be unseen again by night. The Lead's 'a guard wakes' (Q22) is the daytime half.

why_this_origin: Round 2 (Q6) settled the second zone as PINE FOREST WITH CAMP, so the camp is in the forest. Layout inside the forest is still the Lead's.

Placed ~14 m from SM_Shrine_Return at (6, -75, -95). The return shrine is the spirit node you come down through; the camp is what you come down FOR. Proximity makes the portal read as a door rather than a teleport.
locked_signature: jagged asymmetric wedge, tallest in frame
signature_note: 'Tallest in frame' is read here as RELATIVE dominance - the fire is the tallest thing among its immediate neighbours (0.4 m bedrolls, 0.9 m stakes), not as the band 'tall'. Combat does not need to be tall in itself; it needs to win the frame. This reading is mine and is flagged for the Lead, because ASPECT_BANDS would otherwise read the fire as 'mid' and call it non-conforming.

modules.name: SM_Camp_Bedroll_B
modules.note: Offset 1.2 m along Y from A. Two bedrolls at the same offset would overlap and fail the collision check.

modules.name: SM_Camp_Lashings
modules.role: holds_the_companion - the thing you must calm a guard to reach

actors.label: NODE_GUARD
actors.name: the patroller
actors.what_you_do: reach them unseen, then ease their thoughts
actors.difficulty: the hard one - putting someone to sleep is the act
actors.note: NOT an obstacle. 'Avoid 1 guard' survives as TRAVERSAL, not as the goal - you approach someone you have to reach, without being seen first. See T0_MECHANIC_INVENTORIES_V1 #14.

actors.label: NODE_CAPTIVE
actors.name: the companion
actors.end_state: FREED, and the return leg is reachable
actors.gate: all THREE of the above must be calm

actors_note: Settled 2026-10-02: all three camp actors are CALMED, which corrects the original reading of M14 as 'one obstacle to avoid, two targets to calm'. They differ only in direction - the guard is moved awake-to-asleep, the two sleepers are kept there. Keeping someone asleep is the care; putting them to sleep is the act. That is V2b inside a single must, and it is why there is no efficient version of this beat to choose over the kind one.

visibility.settled: Lead 2026-10-02 - BOTH a light level and a per-actor area, and they are the SAME mechanic.
visibility.rule: Spirit-blue light is visibility. Inside either light radius you are visible to the guard.

sources.what: a tinge of spirit blue in the CENTRE of the campfire
sources.behaviour: a fixed radius where you are visible
sources.radius_note: DELIBERATELY unset. The Lead specified that it exists and that it is dangerous, not how big. Guessing a number here would be authoring gameplay as art.

sources.behaviour: an area around the guard that travels with them, so the safe pocket changes as they walk
sources.radius_note: Same - unset by choice. The moving radius is what makes this non-trivial: a static one is a lookup, a travelling one means reading a moving safe zone.

visibility.why_one_colour_is_right: Both sources are spirit-blue, so the player learns ONE rule - blue means you can be seen here - in a single glance, from the art alone, with no tutorial. That is VISION_BOARD's 'the world announces what it wants by its shape alone' applied to a stealth system: one colour, two forms, static and moving.

triggers.name: EJECT_TRIGGER_GUARD_WAKES
triggers.on_player_enter_with_guard_aware: kidnap the companion; eject player to homestead
triggers.settled: Q22, Lead 2026-10-02 - A GUARD WAKES. This is the first trigger of any kind in T0; there is no death, no capture and no failure state anywhere else in the prototype.
triggers.reads_as: The daytime half of the guard's job. You were seen in daylight, which is why you go home empty-handed.

triggers.name: FREEDOM_GATED_ON_ALL_THREE_CALM
triggers.condition: ALL THREE camp actors must be CALM: the guard asleep, and both sleepers still asleep. Not converted - CALMED.
triggers.settled: Lead 2026-10-02: 'a guard will be awake that you need to help ease their thoughts so that they fall asleep, the other two will be asleep and you can ease their thoughts too to keep them sleeping.'
triggers.widened_from_two_to_three: This was first written as 'both sleepers asleep' before it was known the guard is also calmed and must also be asleep. The count is three.
triggers.why_this_is_the_whole_beat: This is the only condition in the camp that makes M14 non-optional. Until now 'soothe 2 sleepers' was a must with nothing downstream of it - you could skip it and the night still ended. Now skipping it means you stand next to your companion and cannot open the lashings, because three people are awake or unsettled. The calming is not a side objective; it is the lock on the door.
triggers.anti: Freeing the companion with any of the three not calm is a FAIL, exactly as killing one is. There is no force option, and a CONVERTED actor does not count as a calmed one.

triggers.name: NODE_PORTAL_CAMP_ARRIVAL
triggers.on_enter: player arrives in spirit form; spirit-stealth becomes available
triggers.note: Reuses shrine language per the must list. #13.

new_labels_needed: SPIRIT_STEALTH - RESOLVED as must #17. The mechanic is LIGHT-TO-VISIBILITY, not a stat: spirit-blue light makes you visible, from either the campfire's blue centre or the patrolling guard's blue torch. Recorded in T0_MECHANIC_INVENTORIES_V1 #17 and in the visibility block above. Radii deliberately unset.

SLEEPER_STATE_CALM - must #16 needs a state that is NOT EConvertedFoeRole. A converted actor is a defeated foe; a calmed one is someone you helped. Conflating them lets the player defeat the three and unlock the captive, which inverts the beat.
NODE_CAPTIVE - RESOLVED as must #16. The actor and the freedom gate are now specified; what does not exist yet is the code.
open_questions: Q15, still parked: is the clearing ~84 m across as the old measurement suggested, or a smaller one? The ZONE is settled (pine forest with camp); its SIZE is not. The 18 x 18 m above is a placeholder chosen so all four beat nodes and a guard patrol fit with room to walk around them - it is not a recommendation.

Layout inside the clearing - where the fire sits relative to the bedrolls, which side the lashings are on, where the portal opens - is the Lead's. It decides whether the player can see the captive from the portal, which decides whether the rescue reads as a choice or a scripted walk.
Does the lashings read as a cage? A cage invites killing the guard to open it, which inverts the beat. The whole point is that the only way through is to calm them.
measured_note: DELIBERATELY NULL. Nothing here is built, so there is nothing to measure. Every size above is authored from the 1.8 m adult reference and the must labels, and is recorded as 'authored, not built' per module. A reader run will report this assembly as MISSING until it exists - that is the correct report, and it should not be suppressed.
why_this_spec_exists_first: The reader only validates what a spec names. The shrines were in no spec at all, so a shrine with its lintel on the ground and both posts stacked survived every gate until someone measured the envelope by hand.
The camp has THREE prove scripts that currently prove nothing: t0_m8_day_camp_eject_prove.py, t0_m13_portal_camp_prove.py, t0_m14_camp_night_prove.py. They have no geometry to run against.
M8, M13 and M14 are all NO_VERDICT or PROVISIONAL in the must list, and all three are waiting on exactly this.
